newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian lab says Bre-X provided Busang samples.
newsitem.headline: Australian lab says Bre-X provided Busang samples.

text.p: Normet Pty Ltd, the Australian laboratory which analysed original core samples supplied by Bre-X Minerals Ltd from the Busang project, said on Friday it was not the only organisation which identified coarse gold in the Busang samples.

In a statement issued from its Perth headquarters, Normet said its job had been to make a metallurgical, not geological, assessment and the potential presence of alluvial gold in the assay samples had not been a consideration.

"We worked to the client's scope, establishing the best processing route for the deposit they (Bre-X) had identified, and as metallurgists, the geological origin of gold is not within our field of expertise," Normet director Lincoln McCrabb said in the statement, issued by the firm "to clarify its role in the (Busang) project".

"Normet, like Hazen Laboratories who conducted parallel testwork in North America, depend on the legitimacy of samples provided and the information from our client, as well as their geological and mining consultants, to reach conclusions," he added.
"The focus is on us as the only group to have identified coarse gold present, but other laboraties and consultants identified similar findings," McCrabb said.
Normet's scope of work for the project was to manage a metallurgical programme to determine the optimum method for recovering gold from samples supplied by Bre-X, McCrabb said.
"As metallurgists, we have never commented on the source of gold as it is not in our area of expertise," he added.
As part of the testing programme, all samples were ground in a ball mill before gravity recovery and mineralogy. A high gravity recovery was achieved, he said.

Normet's contribution to the overall project was "a small part" compared with all the drilling, geological logging, assaying, resource calculations, process design, engineering and environmental studies that made up the Busang project, he said.
"All testwork reports covering findings of the work were sent to both our client Bre-X and the project manager, Kilborn Engineering," McCrabb said.

"The wealth of knowledge generated from the Freeport-McMoRan Copper and Gold Inc work and the Strathcona (Mineral Services Ltd) report make it easy in hindsight to make comments about the gold origin. However, at the time the work was undertaken there was no indication from consulting geologists or mining engineers involved in the project that the presence of alluvial gold was a consideration," he said.
